## 2. Product scope

The product is a centralized management reporting and analysis system for a large library consortium with many branches and shared library data. Its primary users are library staff, managers, directors, local and global administrators, and other authorized personnel; patrons interact only indirectly through the public catalog or library displays. It supports reporting and analysis for collections, inventory, capacity, circulation, holds, patrons, finances, data quality, transfers, and operational oversight. The product reads and analyzes data from enterprise library-automation modules and integrates with related systems, but does not replace patron-facing catalog functions or manage core acquisitions, cataloging, or circulation workflows.

## 3. Priority scale (MoSCoW)

| Priority | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Must** | Essential; mandated by stakeholders, law or the core purpose. Without it the release fails. |
| **Should** | Important and expected, but a workaround exists or it can follow shortly. |
| **Could** | Desirable improvement (nice to have); included if time and budget allow. |
| **Won't** | Explicitly agreed to be left out of the current release (deferred). |

## 4. Glossary

| Term | Definition | Avoided synonyms |
|---|---|---|
| **Library location** | A branch, facility, or other organizational site at which library materials, staff, transactions, or financial activity are associated. | branch, facility |
| **Library system** | An organizational library entity that contains or administers one or more library locations. | - |
| **Consortium** | The overall network of participating library systems and locations managed through the centralized product. | system-wide |
| **Staff member** | An authorized employee or worker who uses management, reporting, or operational functions. | staff user |
| **Library manager** | A management user responsible for supervising a library location or organizational unit. | branch manager |
| **Local administrator** | An administrator responsible for local configuration, permissions, and reporting for a library system or location. | Local System Administrator |
| **Global administrator** | An administrator responsible for system-wide configuration, permissions, software changes, and consortium-level reporting. | Global System Administrator |
| **Library director** | An executive user who plans and directs library services, priorities, and strategic activities. | - |
| **Patron** | A person whose library account, activity, demographic attributes, or financial obligations are analyzed by the system. | borrower, library customer |
| **Item record** | A record representing a physical or otherwise individually managed library item, including its location, status, condition, value, and circulation history. | item entry, copy record, copy entry |
| **Bibliographic record** | A catalog record describing a title or work to which item records may be attached. | bib record, bibliographic entry |
| **Volume record** | A catalog hierarchy record that groups item records under a bibliographic record in the library system. | volume entry |
| **Uncataloged material** | Library material tracked for inventory or circulation without an individual catalog record. | noncat, non-cataloged material |
| **Report** | A generated presentation of selected, aggregated, or historical library data according to defined criteria. | - |
| **Report template** | A reusable definition of report criteria, fields, formatting, permissions, and output behavior. | report model |
| **Canned report** | A pre-defined report supplied with the product and intended to run with limited modification. | predefined report, pre-written report |
| **On-demand report** | A report generated when requested, using preset logic that may allow selection or display criteria to be changed. | noncanned report, ad hoc report |
| **Open-template report** | A report designed by selecting available record fields, filters, operators, and display options. | - |
| **Query** | A structured specification for selecting, filtering, joining, grouping, or aggregating records. | - |
| **Report queue** | The ordered processing mechanism for submitted reports, including waiting, running, completed, and failed states. | query queue, report job queue |
| **Reporting warehouse** | A data store or reporting environment containing historical or otherwise separated data for reporting without disrupting operational processing. | reporting database |
| **Circulation transaction** | A recorded event involving the lending, return, renewal, or use of library material. | circ transaction, circulation activity |
| **Checkout** | A circulation transaction that lends an item to a patron or records an equivalent use. | check-out, check out |
| **Renewal** | A circulation transaction that extends the loan period of an item. | - |
| **Hold** | A patron request to reserve or obtain an item or title when it becomes available. | request |
| **In-transit item** | An item recorded as moving between a sending and destination library location and not yet received. | transferred item |
| **Item transfer** | An operation that changes the assigned location of one or more items and may coordinate their physical movement. | batch transfer, transfer utility |
| **Collection capacity** | The measured ability of a library location or system to accommodate items, shelf space, circulation workload, or processing volume. | branch capacity, capacity status |
| **Shelf space** | The physical or estimated space occupied or required by a collection of items. | - |
| **Material volume** | The quantity of library material calculated from acquisitions, items at their library location, and items in circulation. | volume of material |
| **Collection weeding** | The process of identifying and removing, discarding, or changing the status of items according to collection-management criteria. | purging |
| **Deletion audit** | The audit record of deleted records, including the record type, identity, actor, time, location, and related details. | deletion log |
| **Financial transaction** | A recorded monetary event involving patron charges, fines, waivers, payments, bills, or ecommerce activity. | financial activity, payment transaction |
| **Role-based access control** | Authorization in which permissions are assigned through security groups or roles rather than individually managed permissions. | RBAC, role-based permissions |
| **Personally identifiable information** | Information that can identify or be linked to an individual patron. | PII, personally identifying information |
| **MARC** | A machine-readable bibliographic record format whose fields may be selected, displayed, or validated in reports. | - |
| **Online Public Access Catalog** | The patron-facing catalog interface through which patrons search library holdings and may perform supported account activities. | OPAC, public catalog |

## 5. Requirements

### Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

#### REQ-001: Save And Share Queries

**Priority:** Must (The requirement is described as 'crucial' and 'need', indicating essential functionality.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-04, DOC-15, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-055, C-056, C-057, C-536, C-695, C-707

The system shall allow users to save and share queries for repeated use so that staff members can reuse commonly run queries and share them with colleagues. Saved queries support recurring operational workflows such as monthly runs and can be treated similarly to Report templates for distribution and reuse. This feature improves efficiency by avoiding repeated query construction.

#### REQ-002: Staff Productivity And Workflow Analysis

**Priority:** Should (No explicit mandatory wording; described as an analytical capability expected by stakeholders.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-17 · **Candidates:** C-184, C-586

The system shall support analysis of staff member productivity and workflow so Library managers and administrators can assess operational efficiency and staff activity patterns. Analysis shall use staff-related operational data to report on productivity and workflow metrics.

#### REQ-003: Local Administrator Configuration

**Priority:** Should (The evidence describes expected administrative capabilities without mandatory wording, so assign Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-17 · **Candidates:** C-186, C-592

The system shall allow Local System Administrators to configure local settings and run system reports so individuals who oversee Library processes at the Library location can adapt settings and produce reports for their Library location. Local System Administrators shall have the elevated permissions necessary to perform local configuration and reporting tasks.

#### REQ-004: Manager Reporting For Planning

**Priority:** Should (No mandatory cue; requirement describes expected reporting support for managers.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-187

The system shall provide reports for Library Managers to support planning and evaluation so managers can use report outputs to make operational and programmatic decisions for their organizational units. Reports shall target the planning and evaluation needs of Library managers.

#### REQ-005: Aggregated Reports For Directors

**Priority:** Should (The evidence describes an expected capability for directors but uses non-mandatory language, so assign Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-188

The system shall provide aggregated, high-level reports for library directors to support strategic planning and board presentations, delivering summarized metrics and trends appropriate for executive decision-making. These aggregated reports shall enable library directors to prepare materials such as board reports and strategic analyses across the consortium and constituent Library locations.

#### REQ-006: Report Template Creation And Management

**Priority:** Should (Cue: 'need/needs to' indicates an expected capability but not explicitly mandatory in constraint language.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12, DOC-14, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-194, C-422, C-479, C-523, C-691

The system shall allow system administrators to create report templates that are available to staff members and can be run as-is or modified for individual needs so administrators can publish consistent starting points while letting staff tailor display where permitted. Template management shall support template availability and the ability to run templates without modification or with permitted edits.

#### REQ-007: Run Or Customize Report Templates

**Priority:** Should (The evidence states this as an expected capability without mandatory language, so assign Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-195, C-376, C-474

The system shall allow users to run report templates, including canned reports, as-is or to modify their permitted display options for individual needs so staff users can either execute predefined reports or adjust display settings where allowed. Modifications shall be limited to display options permitted by report permissions while preserving the underlying canned report definitions.

#### REQ-008: Template Change Integrity

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; maintains important quality attribute of consistency tied to stakeholder concern.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12 · **Candidates:** C-196, C-423, C-427

The system shall ensure that changes to report templates do not compromise the accuracy or consistency of their results and criteria so that standardized reports produce consistent outputs across users and time. Template editing and versioning shall preserve result accuracy and allow consistent replication of named reports.

#### REQ-009: Fine-Grained Report Permissions

**Priority:** Should (Stakeholders stated 'We need' fine-grained permissions; requirement framed as necessary but without absolute mandatory phrasing.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12, DOC-14, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-199, C-377, C-428, C-480, C-692

The system shall provide distinct, fine-grained permission levels that limit who can create, clone, or add canned reports so that the ability to manage report content is controlled by role and permission. Permission controls must distinguish among actions such as creating new reports, cloning existing reports, and adding canned reports, ensuring only authorized Staff members and administrators can perform those actions. This supports governance of report proliferation and quality control.

#### REQ-010: Shared Folders For Report Access

**Priority:** Should (Sources state administrators 'should' be able to create shared folders; described as a needed administrative control without mandatory phrasing.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12, DOC-14, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-201, C-429, C-521, C-693

The system shall allow system administrators to create shared folders that control which Staff members may run specific reports and which sets of data Staff members may run on-demand reports against, enabling administrators to manage report visibility and data scope per group. Shared folders function as an access and scoping mechanism to permit or restrict report execution and ad hoc query targets for defined staff groups. This supports controlled distribution of reports and data access across the organization.

#### REQ-011: User-Friendly Query Designer

**Priority:** Should (Sources describe this as a desired interface capability ('should', 'We need') but not framed as an absolute mandate.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12, DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-202, C-205, C-206, C-207, C-208, C-209, C-419, C-420, C-458, C-459, C-461

The system shall provide a user-friendly interface for designing queries against bibliographic records, item records, patron records, circulation transactions, and financial transactions, allowing Staff members to select fields, select values from picklists, select regular expressions from a drop-down menu, and use Boolean operators. The query designer must expose the relevant record types and let staff build queries via field selection, picklists of possible values, regex selection, and Boolean composition to produce report datasets. This enables staff to create reports without direct SQL coding while supporting expressive query capabilities.

#### REQ-012: Control Access To Query Tool

**Priority:** Should (Sources explicitly use 'should' to describe administrative control of query access.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12 · **Candidates:** C-203, C-210, C-421

The system shall allow administrators to control Staff member access to the query tool, including access to the database tables and fields used by the query tool, so that data exposure via ad hoc queries is limited by role and permission. Administrators must be able to restrict which tables and fields each staff account or role can query to enforce data governance and privacy policies. This supports security and compliance while enabling authorized analysis.

#### REQ-013: Canned Board And Executive Reports

**Priority:** Should (The evidence indicates these reports 'should' be provided and references statutory reporting needs, supporting a Should priority.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12, DOC-18 · **Candidates:** C-204, C-211, C-432, C-630

The system shall provide canned Board and Executive reports for library boards and other external consumers, including the basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid. These predefined reports shall present the standard statistics and formats used for board presentations and external reporting requirements.

#### REQ-014: Display Query Selections With Results

**Priority:** Should (Reviewer and evidence indicate this is a recommended behavior (uses wording 'should'); therefore rated Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12, DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-227, C-437, C-473

The system shall present the query selections used to generate a report alongside the report results so staff members can see the criteria that produced those results and validate or reproduce the query in the future.

#### REQ-015: Report Queue Position And Status

**Priority:** Should (The evidence uses non-mandatory language (needs to, should) and describes an important usability improvement, so rated Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12, DOC-14, DOC-18, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-228, C-438, C-439, C-440, C-442, C-462, C-524, C-629, C-694, C-700

The system shall allow staff members to view their report's position in the Report queue, its status (for example waiting, running, completed, failed), submission time, and priority information so staff can understand queue progress and reduce unnecessary support contacts.

#### REQ-016: Support Appendix A Reporting Definitions

**Priority:** Must (The evidence explicitly states 'must' for supporting the Appendix A reporting definitions, making it mandatory.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-229

The system shall support the reporting definitions described in the report examples in Appendix A, implementing the report definitions and metrics as specified in that appendix so report outputs match the provided examples. This ensures conformity between the system's reports and the documented reporting definitions.

#### REQ-017: Support Appendix B Fine-Grained Reports

**Priority:** Must (The statement and evidence include explicit 'must' indicating an essential requirement.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-230

The system must support the fine-grained reporting requirements described in Appendix B so staff members can produce the detailed, granular reports specified in the attached specification.

#### REQ-018: Three Reporting Interface Types

**Priority:** Should (The statement uses 'shall' to specify needed functionality but does not indicate a legal or essential mandate, so it is classified as Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-360, C-361, C-362, C-363, C-364, C-365, C-366, C-485, C-486, C-522

The system shall provide three reporting interfaces: (a) Canned reports consisting of pre-delivered report templates that users can select and run immediately or on recurring schedules, (b) on‑demand reports consisting of preset reports whose selection criteria and display options users can edit and run on demand, and (c) open-template reports that allow users to select attributes associated with circulation transactions, Patrons, items, financial transactions, and bibliographic records for filtering and display; these interfaces enable Staff member, library manager, Local administrator, and Global administrator to produce both standard and customized reports from the Reporting warehouse. The interfaces are intended to support centralized reporting and analysis without replacing core operational systems.

#### REQ-019: Hover Tooltip For Report Titles

**Priority:** Should (Requirement evidence indicates the feature is currently missing and is needed (No), so it is important and expected but not phrased as mandatory.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-367, C-475, C-476

The system shall provide a quick-access interface that displays a descriptive pop-up when a Staff member hovers over the title of a canned report or report template, so that Staff members can see the report description without opening the report. This feature shall present the description in a small pop-up box directly tied to the report title in the report listing. The pop-up tooltip supports faster selection of appropriate reports and reduces navigation overhead when choosing predefined or template reports.

#### REQ-020: Selectable Data Elements Retain Nulls

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-368

The system shall allow users to select the data elements to include in a report and shall retain null and blank fields in the resulting report data regardless of filtering or display choices so exported datasets preserve the full schema and missing-value information. This enables downstream processing, data quality analysis, and consistent imports into other systems. Users with reporting permissions shall be able to choose which elements appear while the system preserves nulls and blanks for included elements.

#### REQ-021: Scheduling And Recurring Report Editing

**Priority:** Should (Evidence shows current lack of capability and specifies needed functionality (No, needs to), making it important but not framed as legally mandated.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-369, C-373, C-468, C-469, C-525, C-698

The system shall allow a Staff member to schedule reports to run immediately (Run ASAP) or on recurring intervals of hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly, and shall allow Staff members to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and by editing associated email addresses. The scheduling controls shall present the listed frequency options and provide an edit interface for existing recurring report definitions including the recipient email list and included report selections. This capability enables automated distribution and ongoing maintenance of recurring report configurations.

#### REQ-022: Report Output Formats

**Priority:** Must (Evidence explicitly states these formats are required (Excel, HTML, and CSV formats are required).)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-19, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-370, C-671, C-696

The system shall provide report output in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats so that Staff members can receive and consume report results in these widely used file types. The export functionality shall allow reports to be generated and downloaded or delivered in any of the three specified formats. Supporting these formats ensures compatibility with common analysis and presentation tools.

#### REQ-023: Email Distribution And Address Book

**Priority:** Could (The evidence describes this as desirable ('would be great'), indicating an optional enhancement.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-371, C-372, C-470, C-471, C-697

The system shall allow a Staff member to enter email addresses for report distribution and shall deliver scheduled reports by email; the system shall also maintain an address book of regularly used addresses for distribution convenience. Staff members shall be able to specify recipient addresses when scheduling or editing report deliveries and select from saved addresses for repeat use. This capability facilitates automated distribution of report outputs to intended recipients.

#### REQ-024: Configurable Comparative Columns

**Priority:** Should (The requirement is an expected analytic capability without mandatory wording, so Should fits.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-374

The system shall allow a Staff member to configure comparative report columns, enabling output columns such as prior-period circulation counts, prior-year circulation counts, and percentage differences between periods so that comparative trends are visible in a single result set. The configuration shall permit selecting which period columns to include (for example last month, previous month, previous year) and specifying computed percent-difference columns. This supports analysis of circulation trends across different timeframes.

#### REQ-025: Report Queue Prioritization

**Priority:** Must (The evidence labels the ability to prioritize reports as crucial and provides a concrete critical example ('crucial').)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12, DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-379, C-441, C-463

The system shall allow a Staff member to prioritize certain report types so they move ahead of resource-consuming reports in the report queue, enabling higher-priority reports (for example a director's board report) to jump ahead of less critical ad-hoc queries. Priority controls shall affect the ordering in the report queue so prioritized report jobs are scheduled or executed before lower-priority, resource-intensive jobs. This ensures critical reports are delivered promptly despite competing workload.

#### REQ-026: Upload Filter Values From Text File

**Priority:** Should (Evidence indicates the capability is missing (No) and desirable; it is important but not explicitly mandated.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-382, C-472

The system shall allow a Staff member to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs for use as report filters so that bulk identifier-based filtering is supported. The uploaded file contents shall be applied as filter values for report generation, enabling reports to be run against the supplied list of identifiers. This feature streamlines reports that target large lists of items or records identified externally.

#### REQ-027: Pivot Table Output

**Priority:** Should (Evidence notes the feature is currently missing and desirable (No), making it an important capability but not labeled mandatory.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-384, C-465, C-713

The system shall provide pivot table output for reports so Staff members can analyze aggregated data across dimensions within the reporting interface or export pivot-ready results. Pivot output shall allow aggregation and cross-tabulation of report data to support multidimensional analysis. Providing pivot-format results enables flexible summarization and exploration of report data.

#### REQ-028: Proven Output Format Reliability

**Priority:** Should (The statement is a quality expectation without explicit mandatory language, so Should is appropriate.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-385

The system shall provide tested and proven output formats for reports so that Staff members can rely on the stability and correctness of exported report files. Output formats shall be validated to ensure they conform to expected structure and encoding for intended consumption by analysis tools and recipients. Ensuring tested output formats reduces risk of format-related failures when distributing or processing reports.

#### REQ-029: Cancel Scheduled Or Running Reports

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14, DOC-19, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-386, C-464, C-674, C-715

The system shall allow users to cancel a scheduled or currently running report and shall check for cancellation signals during report processing so that users can stop unwanted or obsolete report jobs. The system shall provide the ability to request cancellation for scheduled jobs and running jobs and the report processor shall poll or otherwise detect cancellation signals during execution. This capability reduces wasted processing and supports operational control by staff and administrators.

#### REQ-030: Real-Time Reporting For Current Data

**Priority:** Should (Evidence notes some reports need real-time data and current lack of capability (No), making it important but not framed as mandatory.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14, DOC-19, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-388, C-466, C-672, C-714

The system shall provide real-time reporting for reports that require current data so that Staff members can obtain up-to-the-moment information for time-sensitive queries such as items overdue today. Real-time reporting shall return results based on the current state of the source systems rather than only historical snapshots when the report requires immediacy. This capability supports operational decisions that depend on current system state.

#### REQ-031: Historical Reporting Via Reporting Warehouse

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14, DOC-19, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-389, C-467, C-673, C-712

The system shall provide historical reporting through a reporting warehouse that allows data to be retrieved for a specified date or date range and preserves the historical state of data even when the shelving location has changed so users can view past states of records. The reporting warehouse shall allow queries for data as of a given date range and preserve attributes such as shelving location as they existed on that date. This supports audits, historical analysis, and accurate past-state reporting for staff and administrators.

#### REQ-032: Defined Report Selection Criteria

**Priority:** Should (The statement is an expected quality attribute without explicit mandatory wording.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-390

The system shall clearly define report selection criteria so that Staff members understand precisely which records and fields are included when running a report. Selection criteria descriptions shall be presented in the reporting UI and included in report metadata or headers to reduce ambiguity about the data returned. Clear definition of selection criteria improves reproducibility and interpretation of reports.

#### REQ-033: Include Report Name And Date Range

**Priority:** Should (The requirement is a standard expectation for reporting outputs without explicit mandatory language.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-391

The system shall include the report name and the selected date-range criteria in report results so that Staff members can quickly identify the report and the period covered when viewing outputs. The report metadata shall appear at the top or bottom of the results and explicitly show the date selection used to generate the report. This ensures clarity when reviewing or distributing report outputs.

#### REQ-034: MARC Fields On Single Row

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; the evidence states a clear reporting need without mandatory phrasing.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-394, C-704

The system shall allow report templates to pull specified MARC fields and present those MARC fields on a single row of report data. This enables report consumers to see all requested bibliographic data for a bibliographic record in one row rather than spread across multiple rows. It supports easier analysis and export of bibliographic fields in reports.

#### REQ-035: Transaction Filters By Time Workstation Staff

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; the evidence describes an important but not legally mandated reporting capability.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-395

The system shall allow users to run reports that filter circulation transactions by specified date and time, by workstation, or by staff member. This enables auditors and managers to locate transactions that occurred at particular moments or by particular staff members for operational review and investigation. The feature is used for transaction-level reporting and oversight.

#### REQ-036: Clone Report Templates

**Priority:** Should (The evidence uses the word 'need' indicating an expected capability but not a legal mandate.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-12 · **Candidates:** C-426

The system shall allow users with the appropriate permission to clone an existing report template by creating a new report template based on that existing template. Cloning enables users to reuse report definitions and modify copies without altering the original template. This supports efficient creation of similar reports while preserving approved templates.

#### REQ-037: Expose Database Fields For Reporting

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; the evidence highlights a functional limitation that should be addressed.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-14, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-460, C-703

The system shall make all database fields available for field selection in the report writer, subject to administrator-controlled access restrictions so that report authors can select needed fields while administrators restrict sensitive fields. This capability addresses current limitations where some database fields are not selectable and enables more complete filtering and reporting. Administrators retain control over which fields individual users may access in reports.

#### REQ-038: Background Processing And Queuing

**Priority:** Must (The evidence describes a major concern and states the system needs background processing/queuing to prevent report generation from slowing production.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-14, DOC-16, DOC-18 · **Candidates:** C-478, C-561, C-563, C-607

The system shall provide background processing and report queuing so long-running reports are processed without slowing down the circulation client or other production workflows. Queued background processing ensures complex or resource-intensive reports run asynchronously against reporting infrastructure and do not tie up production resources. This protects operational responsiveness while allowing users to run complex analytical queries.

#### REQ-039: Staff Report Content And Design

**Priority:** Should (No explicit mandatory wording; described as the role of staff members and expected functionality.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-17 · **Candidates:** C-591

The system shall allow staff members to create report content and design services reflected in reports so that paid employees of PINES member libraries can author and shape reporting outputs. This capability enables staff members to be primary content creators for report templates and to configure how services are described and measured in reports.

#### REQ-040: Library Manager Supervision Support

**Priority:** Should (The requirement uses 'shall' but describes organizational responsibilities rather than an externally mandated need; assign Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-17 · **Candidates:** C-593

The system shall allow Library Managers to supervise a single organizational unit and provide input to the design and implementation of library services by enabling access and reporting appropriate to a manager's supervisory scope. The system must therefore provide Library Managers with report access and tools scoped to their single organizational unit so they can review operations and contribute to service design and implementation. This supports managers' responsibilities for unit-level oversight and participation in service decisions.

#### REQ-041: Support Directors Planning And Direction

### Collection, Inventory, Capacity, and Material Operations

#### REQ-047: Material Volume Report

**Priority:** Should (The statement is presented as a key requirement and 'should' in the evidence, so assign Should.)

The system shall provide a Material Volume Report that, for a selected Library location at any point in time, queries item records whose library location equals the selected Library location and bases counts on new acquisitions, items on the shelf or checked in, and items out in circulation. The report shall group results by configurable categories including adult fiction and board books, show hold counts by category, and allow breakdowns such as total items in the Library location, number of holds, number of adult fiction items, and number of board books. This enables library managers to produce monthly board reports without manual aggregation across multiple screens.

### Circulation, Holds, Transfers, and Item Status

#### REQ-094: Holds As Distinct Metric

**Priority:** Should (The evidence explicitly states 'need' for holds as a distinct metric, indicating an expected capability but not using mandatory wording.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-01 · **Candidates:** C-015

The system shall report the number of holds as a distinct metric so that staff members and managers can see holds alongside total items and category counts. Providing holds as a separate metric supports demand analysis and informs collection and capacity decisions.

#### REQ-095: Batch Item Transfer Utility

**Priority:** Should (The cue explicitly states 'should' and highlights efficiency concerns for large-scale updates.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-04, DOC-10, DOC-15, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-053, C-061, C-062, C-063, C-242, C-243, C-534, C-538, C-709

The system shall provide a utility that transfers batches of selected items between library locations by changing each item's library location field using transaction-safe operations and processing very large updates as smaller sub-batches to avoid database locking. The utility is intended for authorized staff and transfer coordinators to move many item records efficiently and safely, and it must handle large collections (e.g., millions of items) by splitting work into smaller transactions. The implementation shall perform location field updates and record change history as part of the transfer operation.

#### REQ-096: Candidate Transfer Query

**Priority:** Must (The evidence labels this as a 'need' and repeatedly states the requirement to query candidate materials, indicating it is essential.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-04, DOC-15, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-054, C-535, C-706

The system shall provide a query to identify candidate materials for item transfers by selecting item records that meet criteria such as location within a section and circulation inactivity (for example, items in the children's section that have not circulated in six months). The query facility shall allow library managers and staff users to specify the selection criteria needed to surface candidate materials for transfer operations.

**Priority:** Must (The evidence uses 'need', indicating the capability is essential.)

### Financial Reporting and Reconciliation

#### REQ-175: Financial Transaction Tracking

### Data Quality, Retention, Privacy, and Auditing

#### REQ-190: Item Transfer Audit Log

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation word; without cues use Should even though it addresses auditability.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-04 · **Candidates:** C-079

The system shall log all item transfers for audit purposes, recording details of each transfer operation so administrators and auditors can review historical transfer activity. Audit logging is intended for compliance and operational oversight and shall capture who performed the transfer, timestamps, source and destination library locations, and the set of items involved. Logged data shall be retained according to the consortium's retention policy and be available for reporting and investigation.

#### REQ-191: Deletion And Purge Audit Trail

**Priority:** Must (The evidence repeatedly states 'need' and 'absolutely need' for audit/compliance, indicating a mandatory requirement.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-06, DOC-07, DOC-10, DOC-15, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-105, C-111, C-112, C-113, C-114, C-115, C-116, C-117, C-118, C-119, C-121, C-122, C-124, C-125, C-250, C-548, C-711

The system shall maintain an audit trail for all record purges and deletions, including Item, Patron, and Bibliographic records, recording the record type, record identifier, deletion or purge time, deleting user, user location or Library location, prior status, and deletion reason when available, and shall count and track deletions by Library location and Consortium and provide administrative reports of total deletions by period, record type, and Library location, including users with the most deletions; the system shall use a database trigger to log deletions to an audit table to provide evidence for retention-schedule compliance. The audit trail shall support counting and reporting by Library location and Consortium to meet auditing and compliance needs. The logging mechanism shall include a database trigger that writes deletion events to a persistent audit table.

#### REQ-192: Denied Deletion Attempt Tracking

**Priority:** Could (The evidence uses 'would be helpful', indicating this is desirable but not mandatory.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-07 · **Candidates:** C-120, C-123

The system shall track deletion attempts that were denied so administrators can support compliance and troubleshooting by reviewing who attempted deletions, when, and why the attempts were denied. Denied-attempt records shall be retained alongside other audit data for administrative review.

#### REQ-193: Privacy-Protecting Transaction Archive

**Priority:** Should (Sources state 'should' and reference legal privacy protections rather than an explicit 'must' in the requirement text.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12 · **Candidates:** C-214, C-215, C-435

The system shall archive circulation transactions in a form that protects patron privacy as defined by applicable law while providing useful demographic statistics, balancing privacy compliance with analytical needs. Transaction archival must anonymize or otherwise protect personally identifiable information per State Law while retaining aggregated or de-identified demographic attributes needed for reporting. This enables long-term analysis without compromising patron privacy.

#### REQ-194: Data-Quality Item And Bib Reports

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation words in the statement or evidence; it is an important operational capability so rated Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-15 · **Candidates:** C-219, C-551, C-223, C-225

The system shall provide data-quality reports for library staff that identify Item records with an invalid item type, Item records with a long call number, and Bibliographic records that have no associated Item records, so staff can find and correct data problems in the reporting warehouse and source systems.

#### REQ-195: Anonymize Demographic Data

**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-20 · **Candidates:** C-236, C-686

The system shall anonymize data used to produce demographic statistics so that the datasets contain no personally identifiable information, ensuring that information that could be used to identify a patron is deleted before demographic outputs are produced. This protects patron privacy while allowing aggregated demographic analysis for planning. The anonymization applies to all demographic processing for staff and managers.

This supports operational analysis and long-term reporting needs.

This ensures that financial reporting and data retention are auditable and meet jurisdictional requirements.

**Priority:** Should (No obligation cue present; functional reporting requirement so Should.)

The system shall generate an Items Deleted Count report for library staff and managers that summarizes the number of items deleted from the collection over a selectable period. #### REQ-203: Retain Transactions Minus PII Per Law

This enables compliance with law and protection of patron privacy in retained datasets.

This supports security, accountability, and audit investigations across the consortium.

#### REQ-205: Batch Operations And Data Quality

**Priority:** Should (No explicit mandatory wording; requirement emphasized importance but not labeled essential.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-15 · **Candidates:** C-553

The system shall support batch operations and data quality features so that staff members can process large sets of records and improve the accuracy and completeness of consortium data. This capability enables automated or grouped changes and validation routines that reduce manual effort and improve reporting reliability. It supports integration flows that operate on many item records, bibliographic records, volume records, and patron records to maintain data quality across the consortium.

#### REQ-206: Provide Data Quality Reports

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-18 · **Candidates:** C-631

The system shall provide data quality reports so that staff and administrators can identify, monitor, and remediate data issues in patron, item, bibliographic, and related datasets. The data quality reports shall surface completeness, consistency, and other quality indicators for the data elements the system collects and analyzes. This capability supports improved reporting accuracy and operational data hygiene across the consortium.

#### REQ-211: Browser And Client Accessibility

**Priority:** Must (The evidence uses 'must' and 'shall' and marks the requirement as critical for supported clients.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-16, DOC-18 · **Candidates:** C-165, C-164, C-564, C-609, C-610

The system shall be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client and when accessed through a web browser shall support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 and later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 and later so staff members can use the system from supported client environments. Management interfaces shall be reachable via the specified browsers or the Windows-compatible client.

#### REQ-212: Assistive Technology Compliance

**Priority:** Must (The evidence states 'MUST', 'mandatory', and 'non-negotiable' citing legal accessibility compliance.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14, DOC-16, DOC-18 · **Candidates:** C-166, C-483, C-526, C-565, C-566, C-611, C-640

The system shall be accessible with screen-reading software, screen-magnification software, and other assistive technology such as JAWS, NVDA, and ZoomText and shall comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements so staff members with disabilities can use reporting and management functions. Accessibility support shall be implemented across interfaces used by staff members and administrators.

#### REQ-213: Relational Database Back End

**Priority:** Must (The evidence uses 'must' and '[* High Priority]' indicating a mandatory architectural constraint.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-16, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-167, C-559, C-612, C-641, C-643

The system shall use a fully relational database back end that supports complex joins and aligns with the relational structure of the consortium database so staff members and administrators can run advanced queries and reports. The database back end shall be compatible with the relational querying needs of reporting and analysis.

#### REQ-214: Standards-Compliant HTML Output

**Priority:** Must (The evidence is marked '[* High Priority], must' and mandates standards-compliant HTML and accessibility measures.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-16, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-168, C-567, C-568, C-613, C-645, C-646, C-647

The system shall produce standards-compliant HTML output for web-based components that is compatible with different browsers and assistive technologies, using properly structured elements including alternative text, ARIA labels, and semantic HTML, and all HTML output shall validate against W3C standards. This ensures web interfaces for staff members and administrators meet accessibility and interoperability expectations.

#### REQ-215: Environment Separation And Migration

**Priority:** Should (The evidence indicates 'need' and '[* Medium Priority]', so it is important but not marked as mandatory.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14, DOC-16, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-169, C-481, C-482, C-528, C-573, C-574, C-614, C-648, C-649

The system shall provide separate development, training, and production environments and shall support export and import of report templates, permission settings, saved queries, and other configurations for migration to the production environment so administrators can manage and promote configuration changes safely. The capability shall enable configuration migration from development and training to production.

#### REQ-216: Role-Based Permission Assignment

**Priority:** Must (The evidence uses '[* High Priority], should' and emphasizes role-based control as a required approach to permissions.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-13, DOC-16, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-170, C-449, C-450, C-451, C-452, C-454, C-572, C-652

The system shall allow administrators to change a staff member's permissions by modifying the staff member's role assignment rather than editing individual permissions so administrators can manage user rights through roles and security groups. When a staff member authenticates, their permissions shall be determined by their assigned role or security group.

#### REQ-217: No OPAC Impact During Reporting

**Priority:** Must (The evidence uses strong mandatory language ('absolutely cannot, must not, shall not') indicating this is essential.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-16, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-171, C-575, C-616, C-654

The system shall not constrain functionality or features of the Online Public Access Catalog or slow down patron access to the Online Public Access Catalog while reports are running, ensuring that reports executed by staff users do not degrade patron-facing services. Reporting operations shall query OPAC data where needed but must not modify OPAC data or negatively affect OPAC performance during patron use.

#### REQ-218: Accessible HTML Help System

**Priority:** Must (Cue: 'No, [* High Priority], critical, has to be' indicating mandatory, high priority.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14, DOC-16, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-174, C-484, C-576, C-619, C-658, C-659

The system shall provide an online, hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable, easy-to-navigate HTML help system that describes and illustrates all system functions and works with screen readers so that staff members can find procedural and feature guidance without contacting IT. The help system shall be organized hierarchically, include cross-links between topics, and support search and screen-reader compatibility for accessibility.

#### REQ-219: Detailed Administrative Error Feedback

**Priority:** Should (Requirement uses 'shall' and explicitly targets administrator roles but is described as medium priority in the source.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-175, C-620, C-660, C-661

The system shall provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback and low-level query-specific feedback through the front-end interface for Local administrators and Global administrators, including the table, field, and type of error when a report fails. This functionality helps administrators diagnose and correct failed reports by exposing both summary-level and specific query error details in the user interface. The feedback must be visible to the appropriate administrator roles to support rapid troubleshooting.

#### REQ-220: Rely On Enterprise Data Structures

**Priority:** Must (Cue: Constraint statement that the system 'shall be part of and rely on' enterprise system, indicating essential integration.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-177, C-621, C-623, C-662, C-664

The system shall be part of and rely on the data structures and functionality of an enterprise library-automation system, including reading data from its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, so reporting and analysis reflect canonical enterprise data. The management reporting system shall use the enterprise library-automation system data structures as its source of truth for acquisitions and cataloging information.

#### REQ-221: Centralized Consolidated Deployment

**Priority:** Should (The evidence states the consolidation requirement but does not use explicit mandatory legal wording, so assign Should.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-178, C-622, C-663

The system shall be consolidated at a central location, accept input from multiple Library locations, and provide services to multiple Library locations so that management processes operate centrally while serving the consortium's branches. Centralized consolidation enables consistent reporting and management across Library locations.

#### REQ-222: Vendor Integration Via Standard Interfaces

**Priority:** Must (Cue: Constraint specifying required interface methods ('shall interface ... via published APIs and/or automated transfer').)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-179, C-624, C-665

The system shall interface with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfers of standard-format data files, including USMARC21 and EDIFACT, to enable exchange of acquisitions and cataloging data with external vendors. Interfaces shall use published APIs or automated standard-format file transfers to ingest or exchange vendor-supplied data.

#### REQ-223: Read-Only OPAC Interaction

**Priority:** Should (The evidence describes this interaction as a required design constraint but uses descriptive rather than legally mandatory wording, so assign Should.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-17, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-180, C-590, C-625, C-668

The system shall interact with the Online Public Access Catalog by querying its data, including patron data such as holds and circulation transactions, and shall not modify Online Public Access Catalog data. This ensures the reporting system obtains necessary patron and circulation information from the OPAC while preserving the OPAC as the authoritative source for patron-created data.

#### REQ-224: Global Administrator System Functions

**Priority:** Should (The evidence defines the Global System Administrator role and expected functions but does not include mandatory wording, so assign Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-17 · **Candidates:** C-189, C-595

The system shall provide Global System Administrators with functions to implement software changes and configurations and to generate statistical reports for the entire consortium, enabling consortium-level administration and reporting. Global System Administrators shall have access to consortium-wide configuration and reporting tools to manage the centralized system.

#### REQ-225: Optional Streamlined Logins

**Priority:** Should (The evidence explicitly states the streamlined method 'should' be supported but optional, indicating Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-13 · **Candidates:** C-190, C-192, C-443, C-444, C-446, C-456, C-457

The system shall support, but not require, streamlined methods of logging into terminals, such as card swipe, alongside individual username-and-password login so staff users may use faster terminal sign-in methods while preserving individual authentication alternatives. Streamlined login methods shall be optional and coexist with traditional individual credential login.

#### REQ-226: Badge Swipe With Individual Auth

**Priority:** Should (The evidence emphasizes the streamlined method should not bypass authentication but uses advisory wording ('shouldn't'), so assign Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-13, DOC-18 · **Candidates:** C-191, C-445, C-632, C-448

The system shall allow staff members to use an employee badge swipe or other streamlined login method to identify themselves and initiate login, but the streamlined method shall not bypass individual authentication entirely; staff shall still be authenticated through individual credentials or an equivalent individual authentication mechanism. This ensures convenience while maintaining individual accountability for staff users.

#### REQ-227: Easy Permission Administration

**Priority:** Should (Requirement described as 'need' and emphasizes ease of administration rather than an absolute mandate.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12 · **Candidates:** C-200, C-430

The system shall make report and system permissions easy to administer so that administrators can manage access rights efficiently and accurately across staff roles and library locations. Permission management tools should minimize complexity and administrative overhead while supporting the required fine-grained controls. This reduces the burden on Local administrators and Global administrators responsible for access management.

#### REQ-228: Staff Account Password And Expiration Report

**Priority:** Should (The statement uses 'shall' but does not indicate a legal or essential mandate; without such cues the requirement is classified as Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-339, C-515

The system shall generate a report that lists Staff member accounts together with the date of last password change and account expiration for use by Local administrator and Global administrator and other authorized personnel, so administrators can monitor account currency and expirations for operational oversight. The report shall be produced from the Reporting warehouse so it reflects consolidated system data across the consortium. The report is intended for management and audit of staff accounts and does not modify account state.

#### REQ-229: Auto-update Role Permissions

**Priority:** Should (The statement uses mandatory wording 'shall' but no legal or mandatory cue; apply Should as the expected behavior without explicit external mandate.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-12 · **Candidates:** C-431

The system shall automatically update a staff member's report permissions when the staff member's assigned role changes, so that report access reflects the staff member's current role without manual intervention. This ensures that when a staff member is reassigned (for example, from Staff member to Library Manager) their report permissions are adjusted immediately according to the Role-based access control definitions. This behavior reduces administrative overhead and prevents stale permissions from persisting after role changes.

#### REQ-230: Role Support And Permissions

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-13, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-453, C-653

The system shall support roles including Global administrator with full system access, Local administrator with library-location-level reporting and configuration, Library manager with access to run approved reports and limited report-template modification, Staff member with access to run reports within assigned permissions, and Patron with indirect access through Online Public Access Catalog displays so that access and capabilities are aligned with organizational responsibilities. Each role shall have the permissions and access scope described so administrators can assign roles and enforce appropriate boundaries. This supports secure, role-appropriate access for staff, managers, directors, and administrators.

#### REQ-231: Reduce Password Sharing Risks

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; the evidence describes a desired security improvement rather than a mandate.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-13 · **Candidates:** C-455

The system shall reduce security issues caused by password sharing and staff members leaving terminals logged in by implementing controls that discourage shared credentials and detect or prevent unattended sessions. These measures help mitigate the operational security problems that arise when staff rush and share passwords or forget to log out. The system's security controls should improve accountability and reduce unauthorized access.

#### REQ-232: Run Reports On Separate Warehouse

**Priority:** Must (The evidence states the need to separate reporting from production operations to avoid negative impact on production.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-477, C-527

The system shall run reports against a separate reporting warehouse or replica rather than the production database so that reporting workloads do not interfere with live production operations. Using a reporting warehouse protects the circulation client and production services from heavy report queries and supports stable operational performance. Administrators shall manage the reporting warehouse to provide up-to-date read-only views for reporting purposes.

#### REQ-233: WorldCat Integration

**Priority:** Must (The evidence labels WorldCat integration as CRITICAL.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-15 · **Candidates:** C-546

The system shall integrate with WorldCat to support reporting needs that depend on WorldCat data such as last copy determinations and broader bibliographic context. Integration with WorldCat enables the consortium to augment local bibliographic data for reports and decision-making about last-copy status. The evidence identifies WorldCat integration as critical for certain reporting functions.

#### REQ-234: PostgreSQL 8.3 Database Use

**Priority:** Must (Explicit statement that it runs PostgreSQL 8.3 for the database indicates an essential constraint.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-16, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-558, C-642

The system shall use PostgreSQL 8.3 for the database so that the reporting platform runs on the consortium's chosen database technology. This constraint dictates the database engine for storage of reporting and warehouse data and applies to deployments that support the consortium environment.

#### REQ-235: Role-Based Access With Security Groups

**Priority:** Must (The evidence labels this requirement as 'essential' and uses imperative language, indicating it is mandatory.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-16, DOC-18, DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-570, C-569, C-571, C-615, C-639, C-651

The system shall implement Role-based access control using security groups and roles that allow access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups, so permissions can be managed at multiple organizational scopes. Security groups and roles must enable assignment of rights and privileges to single staff members, to defined workgroups, and to ad hoc staff groups for flexible administration. This approach centralizes permission management and supports consistent enforcement of access policies.

#### REQ-236: Configurable Server OS And Browser Support

**Priority:** Should (Described as technical constraints without mandatory wording; expected deployment requirement.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-18 · **Candidates:** C-638

The system shall accommodate configured server operating-system choices and supported web browsers so that the consortium can deploy the reporting system on approved server platforms and provide staff members with compatible browser access. This constraint ensures the product can be installed into varying technical environments and meet local operational requirements.

#### REQ-237: Avoid Denormalization For Reporting

**Priority:** Should (Phrase 'strongly recommend against' signals important guidance but not an explicit mandatory legal constraint.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-644

The system shall not denormalize reporting data because stakeholders strongly recommend against denormalization for reporting to preserve data integrity and simplify maintenance. This constraint directs the data modeling approach for the reporting warehouse and analytics processes across the consortium.

#### REQ-238: Safe Training Environment

**Priority:** Should (The statement expresses a clear need but lacks external mandate language; assign Should.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-650

The training environment shall allow staff members to experiment without risking production data so that staff can learn and test reporting features safely. The environment must isolate training actions from the production reporting warehouse and production data to prevent accidental modification or exposure of live data. This ensures safe practice, onboarding, and experimentation without affecting operational systems.

#### REQ-239: Handle EDI Ordering Data

**Priority:** Should (No mandatory cue; statement notes need but also that data cannot be relied on universally.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-666, C-667

The system shall handle EDI ordering data from vendors when that data is available so that the reporting system can incorporate vendor-provided ordering information into financial and acquisitions-related reports. The system shall accept EDI data when present while accommodating that EDI data may not be available from every Library location.

#### REQ-240: Separate From Online Public Access Catalog

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation language; requirement is a constraint but a workaround may exist.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-669

The management reporting system shall be separate from the Online Public Access Catalog so that the reporting and analysis product does not replace or interfere with patron-facing catalog functions. The system shall integrate with the Online Public Access Catalog for relevant data reads where required but operate as a distinct system for reporting and administrative use. This separation preserves the public catalog's role and limits the product to management reporting and analysis.

#### REQ-241: Read-Only For Acquisitions And Cataloging

**Priority:** Must (Explicit statement that the reporting system doesn't manage those workflows and only reads the data indicates a mandatory boundary.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-19 · **Candidates:** C-670

The system shall not manage Acquisitions or Cataloging workflows and shall only read data from those modules so that core workflow systems remain the authoritative sources. This constraint requires the reporting system to ingest and analyze data from acquisitions and cataloging modules without performing operational management of those workflows.

### General

#### REQ-242: Username/Password Fallback Authentication

**Priority:** Must (The clause 'shall not require' and the authentication constraint create a mandatory security/access requirement, so rated Must.)  
**Type:** non-functional · **Sources:** DOC-10 · **Candidates:** C-193

The system shall allow staff members to log in using individual username and password credentials as a fallback to card-based login and shall not require card-based login, ensuring staff can access the system when card-based authentication is unavailable.

#### REQ-243: Admin Control Over Template Filters And Fields

**Priority:** Should (No explicit obligation words in the statement or evidence; it is an important governance feature so rated Should.)  
**Type:** functional · **Sources:** DOC-10, DOC-12, DOC-14 · **Candidates:** C-197, C-424, C-425, C-520, C-198

The system shall allow administrators to limit which filters and display fields of a Report template staff members may alter, permitting safe changes such as specifying call-number ranges and adding or removing display fields while preventing staff members from altering a Report template to display deleted items, so templates produce certified and dependable outputs.

- [duplicate/medium] REQ-047, REQ-049: REQ-047 already requires configurable categories in the Material Volume Report and hold counts by category. REQ-049 restates those same capabilities.
- [duplicate/medium] REQ-047, REQ-094: REQ-047 already requires the report to show the number of holds as a distinct breakdown; REQ-094 restates that reporting need.
- [duplicate/medium] REQ-127, REQ-128: Both require a combined total circulation report covering cataloged and uncataloged material. REQ-127 adds a type breakdown, but REQ-128's core combined-report need is already covered.
- [duplicate/high] REQ-080, REQ-089: Both require a report of deleted items that were the last copy, including the affected library location. These express the same reporting need.
- [unclear/medium] REQ-152: Requiring patron records with null or blank optional values to appear regardless of filtering makes it unclear how demographic and activity filters are meant to apply; null-valued records could bypass the selected criteria.
- [unclear/medium] REQ-039: “Create report content and design services reflected in reports” does not clearly state whether staff design reports or design library services, so the requirement does not match its name unambiguously.
- [out_of_scope/medium] REQ-205: The requirement extends beyond reporting and data-quality analysis to grouped or automated changes across item, bibliographic, volume, and patron records. This describes broad operational record modification rather than the stated reporting-system scope.
- [wrong_priority/medium] REQ-053: The rationale cites “need/should” language, but assigns Must by treating that wording as essential. The explicit “should” cue aligns with Should on the stated priority scale, absent a stronger mandatory cue.
